title: GC- Overnight Breakout 15M — Phase 2 — Session transitions
summary: Saved Phase 2 session-transition and cohort evidence. This presentation-only supplement preserves research values, frozen selection, unknown outcomes and the earlier reports.

sections.title: Saved evidence and cohort anchors
sections.body: This additive presentation revision exposes existing verified Phase 2 tables. It preserves the frozen policies, selection and research values. Original-breakout cohorts use the first breakout's New York year and original direction. Actual-entry performance uses each candidate fill's New York year, session and direction. A no-fill episode has no invented candidate-entry session. Unknown observations remain distinct from confirmed absence. The original Phase 1 baseline and the earlier Phase 2 report routes remain available.

sections.title: Chronological transition pairs
sections.body: Breakout-to-candidate rows show original-breakout session to actual candidate-fill session. Breach-to-candidate pairs require a chronologically confirmed protected-boundary breach: its latest possible first-breach time is no later than the candidate entry. Breach-to-price-reclaim is a price event transition, distinct from an executed recovery or reversal trade. The saved count and unknown columns are reproduced directly. A zero count is not evidence of financial recovery; unknown is not zero.

sections.description: Saved transition: breakout_to_candidate_entry:reclaim-q000. Unknown is an explicit category; destination rows are not pooled or inferred. The saved unknown count accompanies the destination roster and must not be summed across destination rows.

sections.title: Complete transition download roster
sections.body: The two downloads partition the original transition table in original row order. They include every breakout-to-candidate policy, every breach-to-candidate policy, breakout-to-breach and breach-to-price-reclaim. All original columns are retained, including transition code and anchor. The private revision retains and pins a byte-identical copy of the full original CSV. Neither the downloads nor browser controls calculate combined statistics.
